Each node is labeled with the Manhattan-distance heuristic h, its estimated remaining distance to the target, from 10 down to 0. The returned shortest path, 10 hops along the top row and down the right column, is in the accent color; along it the steps taken plus h always sum to 10." width="100%"} A* is Dijkstra's algorithm steered by a *heuristic*: an estimate of the remaining distance from a node to the target. Nodes that look closer to the target are explored first, so with a good estimate A* finds the same shortest path after visiting far fewer nodes. It is the standard algorithm for route planning on road networks and maps, game and robot path finding, and puzzle solving, where a natural estimate exists (straight- line distance, Manhattan distance on a grid, number of misplaced tiles). The heuristic must never overestimate the true remaining distance (it must be *admissible*); otherwise the path may not be shortest. Without a heuristic, A* is exactly Dijkstra's algorithm. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The endpoints, as IDs or labels. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The endpoints, as IDs or labels. [heuristic]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional function `heuristic(node_id, target_id) -> float` estimating the distance from a node to the target. If `None` (default), every estimate is `0`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. Weights must be non-negative. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int] or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs of a shortest path from `source` to `target`, or `None` if the target cannot be reached. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist or a weight is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A* (Hart, Nilsson and Raphael, 1968) pops nodes in order of $g(v) + h(v)$, the distance so far plus the estimate. With an admissible and consistent $h$ the first time the target is popped its distance is optimal, and the number of nodes expanded never exceeds Dijkstra's. The heuristic is called once per discovered node (results are cached). The path length agrees with NetworkX's `astar_path_length`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 6 x 6 grid with Manhattan distance as the heuristic, A* walks straight toward the corner: ::: {#82598eda .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec grid = ec.Graph().add_grid_2d(6, 6) position = {n: divmod(i, 6) for i, n in enumerate(sorted(grid.get_node_ids(limit=None)))} def manhattan(node, target): (r1, c1), (r2, c2) = position[node], position[target] return abs(r1 - r2) + abs(c1 - c2) ids = sorted(grid.get_node_ids(limit=None)) path = grid.astar_path(ids[0], ids[-1], heuristic=manhattan) len(path) - 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 10 ``` ::: :::
